column3: ACE inhibitors (angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors) are prescription medications that lower blood pressure by blocking the body's production of angiotensin II, a hormone that narrows blood vessels. Participant takes an angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor (captopril, enalapril, lisinopril, ramipril, fosinopril, benazepril, quinapril, perindopril, trandolapril, moexipril). Counts ACE inhibitors alone (ATC C09A) and, for the ACE-inhibitor component, ACE inhibitor plus diuretic pills (C09BA). Use when the variable names ACE inhibitors / ACE-I or the renin-angiotensin 'captopril, enalapril, lisinopril' wording; not for angiotensin receptor blockers (Taking angiotensin receptor blockers), aldosterone antagonists, or a generic antihypertensive variable (Hypertension treatment). Combination pills: a source variable for 'X with diuretics' counts for X and also for diuretics; production carries the ATC combination code as a variant row. Edge case: a variable that lumps ACE inhibitors and ARBs ('ACE/angiotensin II inhibitors') cannot be split and is a judgment call (see questions).

column3: An antihypertensive is a class of medication used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and reduce the risk of serious health problems like heart attacks, stroke, and kidney failure. Participant is taking medication prescribed to lower blood pressure, as reported by a GENERIC variable that does not name a drug class (e.g. 'any blood pressure medication', 'taking meds for hypertension', 'antihypertensives'). Counts any antihypertensive class when the source gives only the generic yes/no. Use when the variable is generic; not for a variable that names one class (ACE inhibitor, beta blocker, diuretic, ...): those go to the class concept (Taking ACE inhibitors etc.). Not for a diagnosis of hypertension (that is the Condition concept Hypertension) and not for 'have you ever been told you have high blood pressure'. Recall window varies (now, past 2 weeks, past 4 weeks): use the variable's own status. Ever-versus-current: only a current/recent use value is PRESENT; 'used to take' and a bare 'ever taken' with no current-use item are HISTORICAL (drug use is an episodic exposure; a chronic Condition is read differently, see the Condition guide condition_status rule). T88 rule: ATC:C02 (antihypertensives) is shared by Hypertension treatment, Taking alpha blockers and Taking centrally acting agents. The concept, not the code, tells them apart, and the SOURCE VARIABLE decides the concept: a generic 'blood pressure / hypertension medication' variable is Hypertension treatment only; a variable that names alpha blockers (prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin) is Taking alpha blockers; a variable that names centrally acting agents (clonidine, methyldopa, guanfacine) is Taking centrally acting agents. A generic variable is not evidence of a specific class.
